title: Claims Manual: First Notice of Loss under the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy
content:
**Opening a claim.** Under the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy a claim is opened for each occurrence the named insured reports, with the date of loss and the cause of loss as reported. The claim number is assigned at first notice, and every later entry of the claim carries that claim number. A claim number is never opened twice for the same occurrence: where the policy already carries a first notice for the same date of loss and cause of loss, that occurrence already has its claim.

## Coverage on the date of loss

The date of loss falls within a term during which the policy was in force. The date of loss is the one the named insured reports; the terms, the cancellation date and any lapse are read from the policy record.

A loss is denied as **not in force on the loss date** when it is dated:

- before the policy's original effective date;
- after the expiration date or after the cancellation date; or
- inside a lapse gap between an expiration and a late renewal.

## Wind and hail reporting period

A wind or hail claim is covered only when it is reported no later than the wind and hail reporting period that starts on the date of loss.

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Date the period starts from | The date of loss as reported on the claim |
| Unit | Calendar days |
| Last day of the period | The date of loss plus the package's wind and hail reporting days |
| Report made on the last day | On time |
| Report made after the last day | Denied as **late notice** for every coverage part of the claim |

Other perils have no fixed reporting period.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical).* With a hypothetical reporting period of 365 days, the last day is the date of loss plus 365 calendar days. A hail loss reported on that last day is on time; a hail loss reported on the day after it is denied as late notice for every coverage part. A burst-pipe loss reported on that same later day is not measured against this period.

## Surface water and flood

Surface water, flood and rising water are never covered by a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy and are denied as **surface water**. Flood is insured only under a separate FloodGuard Private Flood Policy.

## Denial reasons set at first notice

| Circumstance | Denial reason |
|---|---|
| Loss dated outside every in-force term | Not in force on the loss date |
| Wind or hail reported after the reporting period | Late notice, for every coverage part |
| Surface water, flood or rising water | Surface water |
